title: byobot common definitions, v1
description: Shared building blocks for the byobot v1 contract. Dates and times are checked with patterns (not only `format`) so every implementation rejects the same strings.

id.description: An id. New records get UUIDv7s; parts inside a record (blocks, planned efforts) may use any id unique within it.

slug.description: A short lowercase name of letters, digits and underscores, such as a source (`whoop`), an activity (`barbell_back_squat`) or a location (`example_gym`).

activity_id.description: An activity: a library one (`barbell_back_squat`), or one of yours, `x.` and a slug (`x.cable_fly`), so a library addition never takes your id.

uuid.description: A lowercase UUID: v7 for anything authored, v5 for ids derived from other ids.

kind.description: A record kind. Kinds are open: a replica keeps events of kinds it doesn't know.

timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp with the writer's local offset (`Z` only where the local time is UTC).

date.description: A calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the user's local calendar.

zone.description: An IANA time zone name, such as `America/New_York`.

hlc.description: A hybrid logical clock reading: 13 digits of Unix milliseconds, then a 6-digit counter. Compares as text.

code.description: A code from registry.json, or your own prefixed `x.`. A replica keeps codes it doesn't know without converting them.

unit.description: A UCUM unit code, such as `kg`, `[lb_av]` or `/min`.

ref.description: A record, and optionally a part inside it (a planned effort inside a planned session).

time.description: When the thing happened: an instant (`start` only) or an interval. Both keep the offset they were written in; `zone` is added when the writer knows it. Local dates come from these, never from the machine reading them.

measure.description: One measurement: an exact `value`; a range with `min`, `max` or both (only `min` is 'at least', as in AMRAP); or an estimate, a numeric `value` with the bounds it likely lies within. In a plan it is the target; in a log it is what happened. `unit` is one the code's registry entry accepts.

estimate.description: A `value` with bounds: the value must be a number.
